question.text: Real-estate debt is a sizeable chunk of the private debt market per Chapter 9 primarily because:

answer.text: Banks readily fund land acquisition under working-capital lines.
Real-estate debt is explicitly excluded from SEBI (AIF) Regulations.
RBI has mandated that only debt AIFs can fund real estate.

Land acquisition cannot be financed by banks under their construction-finance or working-capital schemes, opening an opportunity for debt AIFs. Additionally, land costs in metro cities often exceed 50% of project cost and collapse of some real-estate NBFCs created a lender vacuum.

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 9: 'Real estate debt forms a sizeable chunk of the private debt market due to the fact that purchase of land cannot be financed by banks under their construction finance schemes or working capital schemes for large developers. Land acquisition financing provides an opportunity for debt AIFs to step in. In recent years, land costs in India skyrocketed in metro cities and often constituted more than 50% of the project cost of a development. Collapse of some established real estate financing NBFCs opened the door for private credit funds.' The Trap: Option A contradicts banking rules. Options C and D invent non-existent restrictions. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C covered this market-structure point. XXI-B (PM) doesn't usually touch real-estate debt since PMs handle listed securities. Manager's Pro-Tip: For land-financing deals, require promoter shares as collateral (preferably listed for liquidity) AND a SPV ring-fence. If only one of the two is available, discount the LTV by 10-15 percentage points.
